tagline: Up the Lake Huron shore, one lighthouse after another.
intro: Where the freeway ends south of Standish, US 23 becomes a two-lane road and turns along Lake Huron. It follows the Saginaw Bay shore through Au Gres, rounds Tawas Bay, and follows the coast on through Oscoda and Harrisville to Alpena, then swings inland past Long Lake and Grand Lake before returning to the water for Rogers City, Cheboygan and Mackinaw City, about 200 miles and 16 lighthouses in all.

The Lake Huron Shores Good Roads Association finished it as the Huron Shores Highway in 1913. At the Standish end, the railroad depot had gone up in 1888, built by local farmers who each brought their own materials.

moments.title: Tawas Point Light
moments.text: The sand kept building the point out into the lake until the first light stood too far inland to be seen, so this 70-foot tower replaced it in 1877.

moments.title: Alpena and Thunder Bay
moments.text: Offshore lies the first national marine sanctuary on the Great Lakes, kept for its shipwrecks, from wooden side-wheel steamers to steel-hulled ones.

moments.title: Old Presque Isle Light
moments.text: Built in 1840 and replaced after 1867 by a much taller tower two miles north, it is said to be haunted by a former caretaker who comes back to light the lamp.
